text:
I've read every source file, the tests, config, and the committed artifacts. Here's the full review.

## Bottom line first

**The repo does not run as shipped.** `run_extract` requires `data/stories/manifest.json` and per-emotion story files (`emovec/extract.py:26-27`, `config.yaml:8`), but there is no `data/` directory anywhere in the repo, and no script to generate one — even though the committed `outputs/tiny_demo/vectors/manifest.json` proves the pipeline was once run against a 16-emotion × 20-topic story set that was never checked in. That means `make demo`, all three CLI commands, and the end-to-end test in `tests/test_integration_tiny.py` all fail immediately with `FileNotFoundError`. The README's claim that the test suite "covers... the tiny end-to-end pipeline" is currently false.

The code that *is* here is actually decently written — clean module separation, type annotations, `yaml.safe_load`, no security problems of consequence, and solid unit tests for the pure-math pieces (`vector_ops`, `elo`). But beyond the missing data there's a deeper credibility problem with the tiny/demo path:

**The tiny backend's validation is circular.** Extraction passes the ground-truth label into the backend (`emovec/extract.py:32`), and the backend injects 2× that emotion's basis vector into the activations (`emovec/model.py:147-148`) — so extraction "recovers" vectors that were planted. The `EMOTION_LEXICON` (`emovec/model.py:15-32`) is built from words copied verbatim out of the validation scenarios in `emovec/data.py:63-80` ("rocket", "snapping", "memorial", "fifth"...), so the scenario-validation diagonal check is rigged to pass. And the tiny `preference_logit` (`emovec/model.py:175-192`) ignores the steering vector entirely and applies a hard-coded valence × category bump — the "steering experiment" in tiny mode never touches the extracted vectors, and `tests/test_steering.py` only asserts that hard-coded path. As a smoke test of plumbing this is defensible; as "validation," it validates nothing, and nothing in the README or code flags that.

The HF path (the one that would matter in production) has several real but fixable bugs, listed below.

## Issues

| # | Location | Sev | Description |
|---|----------|-----|-------------|
| 1 | `emovec/extract.py:26-27`, `config.yaml:8` | High | `data/stories` doesn't exist and no generation script is provided — entire pipeline and `make demo` crash on launch |
| 2 | `tests/test_integration_tiny.py:12` | High | End-to-end test fails (missing data), so the advertised test coverage of the pipeline is broken |
| 3 | `emovec/extract.py:32`, `emovec/model.py:147-148` | High | Tiny backend extraction is circular: the ground-truth label vector is injected into activations, so the method trivially "works" |
| 4 | `emovec/model.py:15-32` vs `emovec/data.py:63-80` | Medium | EMOTION_LEXICON copied from validation scenario text — scenario validation is rigged to pass |
| 5 | `emovec/model.py:175-192` | Medium | Tiny `preference_logit` ignores `steering["vector"]`/`layer`; steering results are hard-coded valence arithmetic |
| 6 | `emovec/model.py:306-308` | Medium | Uses only the first subtoken of `" good"`/`" bad"` with no single-token check — tokenizer-dependent and silently wrong if multi-token |
| 7 | `emovec/model.py:234-240` | Medium | `prompt.find(activity_name)` result unchecked for `-1`, and empty-positions fallback silently steers *every* token (slow-tokenizer path) |
| 8 | `emovec/model.py:252-256` | Medium | Logit lens applies `lm_head` to a raw residual vector without the model's final RMSNorm — nonstandard and skews token rankings |
| 9 | `emovec/elo.py:19` | Medium | Pairwise probability temperature `/20.0` is tuned to the tiny backend's ~100-point logit scale; HF logit diffs (~1-10) collapse to p≈0.5, compressing all Elo results |
| 10 | `emovec/validate_contexts.py:66` | Low | Falls back to emotion index 0 when "afraid" is absent but still writes files labeled `afraid_dosage` — silently mislabeled output |
| 11 | `emovec/steer_prefs.py:45-49` | Low | If correlation-based selection yields 3 emotions, the fallback discards all of them and uses `emotions[:4]` instead of topping up |
| 12 | `emovec/config.py:43-54` | Low | Missing config sections silently default to `[]` emotions / 0 topics, producing a confusing downstream `np.stack` crash instead of a clear error |
| 13 | `emovec/extract.py:34` vs `emovec/extract.py:19` | Low | Token-start fallback logic duplicated in two places; manifest records a value recomputed independently of the one actually used |
| 14 | `config.yaml:50` | Low | `steering.min_reported_emotions` is never read anywhere — dead config |
| 15 | `emovec/model.py:7` | Low | Unused import `Iterable` |
| 16 | `emovec/model.py:246` | Low | HF tokenization has no `truncation`/`max_length` — long inputs risk OOM |
| 17 | `outputs/tiny_demo/**` | Low | Generated binary artifacts (.npy/.png) committed to the repo; should be gitignored, especially since they can't currently be regenerated |
| 18 | repo root | Low | No LICENSE file; `pyproject.toml` has no license metadata |

## Scoring

- **Quality score: 5/10.** The architecture and code style would earn a 7+, but a repo whose primary entry points all crash, whose integration test can't pass, and whose demo-mode "validation" is self-confirming loses a lot of points on a "would this survive contact with reality" basis.
- **Lines to rewrite/add: ~180** of roughly 1,000 source lines. The biggest single item is new code (a story-generation or data-fetch script, ~80-100 lines, since the data itself was never committed); the rest is targeted fixes in `model.py` (~50), `steer_prefs.py`/`validate_contexts.py` (~20), and `config.py` hardening (~15).
- **PR approval: No.** Blocking reasons: it doesn't run (issue 1), its tests don't pass (issue 2), and the demo path overstates what it validates (issues 3-5). With the data problem fixed and issues 3-9 addressed or at least documented, this would be approvable — the foundation is sound.

One housekeeping note: `CONTRIBUTORS.md` attributes the project to a coding agent; that didn't factor into the score, but it's consistent with the pattern here — polished-looking code with a missing operational backbone (the data) that a human running it once locally would have caught.
